_note: Addendum v2 section H. Each puzzle earns the clues listed in 'clues' (section G: evidence only comes from solving). 'hints' are Danny Cole's three levels: 1 a nudge, 2 a specific suggestion, 3 the answer to this puzzle step (never the whole case). Puzzles marked 'draft' get their final hint wording when the puzzle itself is built (Stage F). 'order' is the order Danny suggests them in. 'built': false until the puzzle exists in the game (Stages D and F); Danny only hints about built puzzles.

puzzles.name: Crime Scene Survey
hints: Before we touch anything, we photograph the office, Chief. Start with a few pictures of the whole room, from the doorway.

For each important thing in there, take three pictures: one from far away, one from a couple of steps, and one close up with the little ruler next to it. Put a numbered marker by each thing as you go.

There are nine things to photograph: Pryce's body, the desk with the brandy and the glass, the music box, the bolt on the door, the bars on the window, the corner of the rug, the drawer with the revolver, the calendar and blotter, and the note under the door. Far, middle and close for each one.

puzzles.name: Bench Test
hints: We only have six drops of test chemical, Chief, so let's not waste them on guesses. Half of the instruction chart is torn off. Find the other half first.
The missing half of the chart is on a shelf in the darkroom, in the Operations building. It says chemical B turns blue if there's cyanide, and chemical C reacts to plant poisons.
Put chemical B on the brandy from the decanter and on what's left in his glass. Both turn deep blue: that's cyanide. His heart tonic only goes brown with C, and that's just the doctor's medicine.

puzzles.name: The Safe
hints: Pryce loved riddles, Chief. Have a look at the books on his shelf. One of them isn't really a book.
Inside the hollow book is a riddle with three parts: 'her years', 'the wings' hearts' and 'the minute the sky stopped'. The photo on the wall, the plane's engines and his pocket watch answer them.
The numbers are nineteen, three and seventeen. Turn the dial left to nineteen, right to three, then left to seventeen.

puzzles.name: Telegram and the Hitch
hints: The telegram that brought us here was tapped out in Morse code, Chief. There's a chart of dots and dashes on the radio-room wall. Take it one letter at a time.
Once you've read it, listen to the way each radio operator taps. Everyone's rhythm is a bit different, like handwriting.
Whoever sent our telegram copied Hobbs's little stumble on the letter Q, but slower and too even. It matches the 'unknown' sample, not Hobbs.

puzzles.name: Fuse Panel
hints: The fuse panel needs the radio and the hangar switched on and the mess hall left off. And we've only got so much wire.
Use the shortest wires you can for the radio and the hangar. Leave the mess hall circuit alone.
Power the hangar and the radio, keep the mess hall dark, and don't use more wire than you have. Then have a close look at the reset lever.

puzzles.name: Torn Letters
hints: Somebody tried to burn some letters in that stove, Chief. There are two different kinds of paper in there: cream and pale blue.
Sort the scraps by the colour of the paper first, then by the handwriting, then turn the pieces until the lines of writing run straight.
The cream pieces are a letter to Julian: 'By Saturday we shall be free of him.' The blue pieces are a contract with a forged signature page. Check the clothes-drying rack on your way out, too.

puzzles.name: Darkroom
hints: Developing photos goes in three baths, Chief: developer, then stop bath, then fixer. Keep an eye on the clock.
Leave each picture in the developer for sixty seconds. Check the needle on the enlarger before you expose. If a picture goes wrong, you can try it once more.
Expose when the needle is in the middle, sixty seconds in the developer, then the stop bath, then the fixer. Look at picture four under the magnifier, especially the shelf in the storeroom.

puzzles.name: Fingerprints
hints: We lifted fingerprints from the glass, the decanter and the music box, Chief. Compare them with the prints from everyone's dinner glasses.
Count the points where the prints match, but measure the size as well. How wide a print is matters.
Measure the width of the print. The scarred one is about two centimetres narrower than Captain Strand's hand, so it isn't hers.

puzzles.name: Music Box Latch
hints: That music box plays a little tune, Chief, and the shelf above it has eight books. Seems like a funny coincidence.
Each note of the tune matches a book: the lowest note is book one, the highest is book eight. Pull the books in the order the tune plays.
Pull the books in this order: five, three, one, three, five, eight, five, three.

puzzles.name: Timeline
hints: Let's put the night in order, Chief. Start with the things we're certain of: dinner, the arguments, the door being bolted, the brandy.
Some times are fixed: the door was bolted at twenty-five past nine, and the tune was heard at ten o'clock. Build everything else around those.

In order: dinner at seven; Julian 8:15 to 8:40; the argument on the runway 8:45; Pryce and the doctor 9:10; the bolt 9:25; the toast 9:40; death 9:46; the tune 10:00; the lights out 10:32 to 10:50; the bang 10:45; Julian at the door 11:15; Tamsin's note 11:30; the door broken down 6:10 this morning.

puzzles.name: The Forgery
puzzles.mechanic: UV lamp and magnifier: spot the alterations
hints: There are two weather reports that should be identical, Chief. They aren't. Somebody changed one.
Try the ultraviolet lamp first, then the magnifying glass, then compare the typed letters on both pages.

There are six changes: different ink on 'clear by noon', a '42' rubbed out, a broken letter 'e', a lighter carbon copy, the date, and a clipped signature. That broken 'e' comes from Miss Quill's typewriter.

puzzles.name: Cracked Mount
hints: To find a crack in the engine mount: spray the red dye, wipe it off, spray the white developer, then look. Don't skip the wiping.
Straight lines running side by side are just marks from the machine that made the part. A real crack wanders and branches.
It's the jagged, branching red line on mount number two. Read the tag hanging on it.

puzzles.name: Fuel Ledger Audit
puzzles.mechanic: Read gauges, fill the ledger, find the discrepancy
hints: Read every fuel gauge yourself, Chief, before you believe what the book says.
Compare today's gauge readings with yesterday's entries in the book, one tank at a time.
Tank C reads 188 gallons, but the book says 226. Thirty-eight gallons are missing, and tank C feeds the big Trimotor. Then take a look at the fuel cap on the Waco.

puzzles.name: Beacon Mirrors
puzzles.mechanic: Rotate mirrors to guide a beam
hints: Two of those mirrors in the beacon room are stuck, Chief. Don't waste time on them.
Turn only the mirrors that move, and bounce the light back and forth between them in a zig-zag.
Use mirror two, then mirror four, then mirror one, and aim the beam at the little light sensor.

puzzles.name: The Crates
hints: Crates can only be pushed, Chief, not pulled. Think before you shove one.
First clear a path to the metal plate in the corner, and never push a crate flat against a wall, or it's stuck.
Push the middle crate out of the way first, then the back one, then walk around and push the last one onto the plate. You can do it in fourteen pushes or fewer.

puzzles.name: The Lock
hints: Picking a lock is about listening, Chief. Each pin gives a tiny click when it sets.
Use very light pressure. Work on the pins from the back to the front, and stop as soon as one clicks.
The suitcase has four pins and the desk drawer has five. Back to front, gently: you get three picks before they break.

puzzles.name: Tamsin's Cipher
hints: Her notes are in a simple code, Chief: each letter always stands for the same other letter.
The first three words are 'PAID 200 MONTHLY'. Use them to work out some of the letters. The code word is a name we keep hearing.
The code word is MARIGOLD. The message says: 'PAID 200 MONTHLY. W/R 31 STORM FALSE.' The 1931 weather report about the storm was false.

puzzles.name: The Manifests
puzzles.mechanic: Sort manifest cards against death certificates
hints: There are six passenger cards for the crashed flight, Chief, but only five death certificates. Somebody's paperwork is missing.
Put the cards in order of their seat numbers, then match each one to a certificate.
Seat four, 'C. Pryce, age 19', has no death certificate. Then have a look at the old newspaper.
